knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The manual warns against running the pump dry, which damages the seals and housing and can cause leakage and flooding.
The bleeder is opened before the start and closed once water flows steadily, which shows the air has cleared.
The handbook describes checking for air leaks, confirming the pool has water in it, and retrying in order. Running it empty and forcing it with every valve open both cause damage.

practicalCriteria: Start-up order is followed and each valve change is observed with the pump off
Air bleeder is opened before the start, the observer is clear, and the bleeder is closed at a steady stream
Pump pot is confirmed full before the pump runs, and no dry running occurs
Clean operating pressure is recorded as the reference
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Start-up record from one supervised start-up
Assessor observation sign-off on bleed and valve sequence
Priming attempt log where a priming problem arose
stopWorkCriteria: Pump run dry or with an empty pot
Bleeder closed before a steady stream, or the pump run with the observer standing in the line of the filter
Test cord used as a permanent supply
Filter pressurised with air or gas
